name: Gemeente Rotterdam
description: Design tokens for Gemeente Rotterdam, composed from the Rotterdam Design System (RODS)
_comment_ramp: The role layer (css/tokens/vng.css) addresses colour through a small ramp
of --vng-color-* / --tilburg-color-* names. Those names are the role layer's
INTERNAL vocabulary, not a claim about which municipality a value belongs to —
css/tokens/conduction.css sets --vng-color-blue-500 to Conduction cobalt for
exactly this reason. Substituting the ramp re-brands all 707 var()-derived
Every value below is traced to a RODS token in the `from` field. Where RODS
has no token at that position the value is DERIVED by darkening the nearest
RODS tint, and `from` says so — those are the only invented colours in this
file and there are three of them.

gray-900.from: DERIVED — gray-tint-11 darkened; RODS ramp ends at tint-11

gray-950.from: DERIVED — gray-tint-11 darkened; RODS ramp ends at tint-11

pink-100.from: DERIVED — magenta-tint-01 lightened; RODS has no magenta tint at this position

pink-200.from: DERIVED — magenta-tint-01 lightened; RODS has no magenta tint at this position

_comment_literal_overrides: The role layer hard-codes these colours inside component declarations
instead of aliasing the ramp, so they have no ramp NAME to substitute on.
Without an entry here each one survives into this brand's file as a VNG
colour — which is invisible until somebody recognises the wrong blue.
The generator reports any literal that still has no entry.

#004488.from: rods-color-green-tint-01 — role layer's brand-blue literal becomes Rotterdam green

_comment_semantic: The --nldesign-color-* layer is what Nextcloud's chrome and Portaliq's site
renderer read. It is authored here rather than substituted, because these are
ROLE decisions (what is a link? what is muted text?) and RODS answers them
LINKS ARE BLACK, GREEN ON HOVER. That is RODS, not an oversight:
rods-color-interactive-default resolves to base-black and interactive-hover to
base-green. A blue link would be the generic NLDS default wearing Rotterdam's
palette, which is the failure mode this whole change exists to fix.

_comment_border: TWO border roles, and only one of them is an accessibility surface.
`border` is decorative (card edges, separators) and is RODS gray-tint-04
at 1.48:1 — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 does not reach purely decorative rules.
`border-dark` is the CONTROL boundary and is RODS gray-tint-08 at 3.53:1,
the same value RODS itself gives --utrecht-textbox-border-color. Anything
drawing an input, checkbox or focusable edge must use border-dark; the
contrast test asserts that one and deliberately exempts the decorative one.

_comment_typography: Bolder and ArialforRotterdam are Rotterdam's licensed faces and are NOT
redistributed here. The stack is declared exactly as RODS declares it, so an
instance that has them installed uses them and every other instance falls
through to Arial — which is the fallback RODS itself names.
_comment_component_overrides: Component tokens that NEITHER the upstream brand mapping NOR the shared
role layer defines, so nothing at all would set them.
The card family is the case that forced this section: 16 card tokens are
consumed by the bundled NL Design System CSS and exactly ONE of this repo's
48 token sets defines any of them. Cards are what a search results list is
made of, so on a search page the single most repeated element was the one
element no theme reached. That is pre-existing and fleet-wide; it is fixed
here for Rotterdam because this is the set the portal ships with.
Values are RODS references, so they move with the palette rather than
freezing a hex at this layer.

borderRadius._comment: RODS is a square-cornered system — rods-time-badge-border-radius is the only radius token upstream ships and it is 0. The pill value is kept for the one shape (tag/badge) the role layer renders as a lozenge.
